verses.zh: （上行之诗。）以色列当说：从我幼年以来，敌人屡次苦害我，
verses.en: A song of ascents.[NOTE:1] “Since my youth they have often attacked me,”let Israel say.
notes: Psalm 129. Israel affirms God’s justice and asks him to destroy the enemies of Zion.

verses.zh: 从我幼年以来，敌人屡次苦害我，却没有胜了我。
verses.en: “Since my youth they have often attacked me,but they have not defeated me.

verses.zh: 如同扶犁的在我背上扶犁而耕，耕的犁沟甚长。
verses.en: The plowers plowed my back;they made their furrows long.

verses.zh: 耶和华是公义的；他砍断了恶人的绳索。
verses.en: The Lord is just;he cut the ropes of the wicked.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The precise significance of this title, which appears in Pss 120-134, is unclear. Perhaps worshipers recited these psalms when they ascended the road to Jerusalem to celebrate annual religious festivals. For a discussion of their background see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 219-21.

verses.zh: 愿恨恶锡安的都蒙羞退后！
verses.en: May all who hate Zionbe humiliated and turned back.

verses.zh: 愿他们像房顶上的草，未长成而枯干，
verses.en: May they be like the grass on the rooftops,which withers before one can even pull it up,[NOTE:1]
notes: The background of the metaphor is not entirely clear. Perhaps the “ropes” are those used to harness the ox for plowing (see Job 39:10). Verse 3 pictures the wicked plowing God’s people as if they were a field. But when God “cut the ropes” of their ox, as it were, they could no longer plow. The point of the metaphor seems to be that God took away the enemies’ ability to oppress his people. See L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 187.

verses.zh: 收割的不够一把，捆禾的也不满怀。
verses.en: which cannot fill the reaper’s handor the lap of the one who gathers the grain.

verses.zh: 过路的也不说：愿耶和华所赐的福归与你们！我们奉耶和华的名给你们祝福！
verses.en: Those who pass by will not say,[NOTE:1] “May you experience the Lord’s blessing!We pronounce a blessing on you in the name of the Lord.”
notes: The Hebrew verb שָׁלַף (shalaf) normally means “to draw [a sword]” or “to pull.” BDB 1025 s.v. suggests the meaning “to shoot up” here, but it is more likely that the verb here means “to pluck; to pull up,” a nuance attested for this word in later Hebrew and Aramaic (see Jastrow 1587 s.v. שָׁלַף).
